newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, gold slides further.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, gold slides further.

text.p: New York precious metals tumbled by the close as gold continued its slide, pulling all the precious metals complex to fresh life-of-contract lows apart from palladium which bucked the trend to settle higher.
Continued South African and Australian producer selling coupled with a a U.S. dollar which soared to a 23-month high against the German mark all undermined the yellow metal, analysts said.
February COMEX gold went out $4.10 weaker at $370.90 an ounce, traded $373.90 to $370.70. Cash bullion was quoted at $368.00 to $368.50 in late afternoon dealer trading.
Trading volumes were not heavy, with gold estimated at 25,000 lots compared to last Wednesday's 38,184 lots.
Others said gold tumbled because of funds selling short. North American producers were unsure whether to buy back some of their forward positions or chase the market lower, traders said.
Once COMEX dipped in line with lower overnight levels, activity died down for much of the session.
The Philadelphia gold and silver stocks index was down 2.85 points at 117.34 late afternoon. The Knight Ridder CRB index was also off 1.34 points at 242.02 points.
Greg Drury of Mitsui and Co, USA said if cash gold broke through $368.00 an ounce it could fall to $360.
Although Drury saw no heavy producer selling Monday, there could be some on the way.
"We are expecting more producer selling to come out of Australia related to project finance - hedging-related selling," he said.
William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said producers remained the main enemy of the market. "Producers have lowered their targets and their view does not appear to be a very constructive one."
A feeling that central banks were more inclined to be sellers rather than buyers also fueled bearish sentiment, traders said.
March COMEX silver ended 4.3 cents weaker at $4.742 an ounce, traded $4.77 to $4.72.
The white metals ended mixed, with January NYMEX platinum settling $4.20 off at $375.70 an ounce, near the day's low of $375.40.
March NYMEX palladium settled $1.05 weaker at $117.65 an ounce, off the day's low of $116.00, also the life-of-contract low set last week.
